version: LOCK 35 V1 (9 Nov 2026) - Jisra's people, work and What Jisra says
builds_on: LOCK 32 Jisra and the toll, LOCK 33 Jisra's masjid, LOCK 34 runner. Design reference (not shown): Muslim 102 (whoever cheats is not of us).

jisra.name: Jisra
jisra.text: The river road crosses here on a bridge of boats.

work.label: Carry fish baskets for Umm Hani · 4 coins

people.name: Hamid

lines.wary: Hamid counts coins and does not look up. “Toll is at the near end. Everyone pays.”
lines.friendly: “The river is high this week. Mind the third boat - it rolls.”
lines.warm: “Sit, sit. The boatmen say you are worth knowing. Tea?”

memory: He does not meet your eye. “One coin. Everyone. I heard you the first time.”
“You paid for that family. Generous. Foolish, but generous.”

people.name: Rafiq

lines.wary: Rafiq is retying a rope between two boats. “Walk in the middle. Don't stop on the joins.”
lines.friendly: “Every boat on this bridge belongs to a different family. I keep them roped together - and the families too, some days.”
lines.warm: “When the flood comes, I'll want strong hands on the ropes. Yours, if you're here.”

memory: “A boat nearly drifted last month on a bad rope. You stopped the next one. I won't forget it.”
Rafiq holds up a frayed end. “Snapped in the night. Bashir says he sold it through you.” He walks away.

people.name: Umm Hani

lines.wary: Umm Hani guts a fish without stopping. “Buying or watching?”
lines.friendly: “My baskets are heavy and my sons are lazy. You can carry, I can pay.”
lines.warm: “You eat with us on Friday. No argument.”

memory: “You watched Hamid take three coins from that family and said nothing. Nobody here did either.”

people.name: Bashir

lines.wary: Bashir twists fibre between his palms. “Rope? I have rope.”
lines.friendly: “Good palm fibre from the south. Twice the price of the market rope and worth three times.”
lines.warm: “Watch my stall for an hour if you like. I trust your counting.”

memory: “You lost me a sale. You also kept me from a drowned boatman on my conscience. We are even.”
“Three coins each. Don't tell me where they came from.”

text: Bashir has to fetch fibre from the far bank. “Watch the stall. Six coins a coil. That one on the end is the old one - it frays a little. Sell it if you can.”
A boatman comes up and points at the old coil. “For my mooring. It has to hold in a flood.”

told.text: The boatman looks at the frayed end, nods slowly and buys a new coil instead. When Bashir comes back he frowns at the old coil still on the end.

sold.text: The boatman pays six coins and carries it off. Bashir comes back pleased and gives you three of them.

told: Told a boatman the rope was weak
hid: Sold a bad rope for Bashir

line: Spoke up to Hamid at the toll
